title: The Glaciers of Kilimanjaro
excerpt: Kilimanjaro still has glaciers near the equator, but they are shrinking fast. What you see on the summit and why it is changing.
body:
One of the most remarkable things on the summit of Kilimanjaro is ice. Near the equator, at almost 6,000 m, glaciers and ice cliffs still survive.

## What you see

From Stella Point and Uhuru Peak you can see the remains of glaciers such as the Southern Icefield, the Rebmann and the Furtwängler Glacier. The vertical ice walls are a striking sight in the morning light.

## Shrinking ice

Since the early 20th century, the ice on Kilimanjaro has shrunk dramatically. Scientists point to a combination of a drier climate, less snowfall and changes in cloud cover, alongside rising temperatures. Several studies have suggested the remaining ice may largely disappear in the coming decades.

## Respect the ice

Do not walk on or touch the glaciers. Ice walls can collapse, and the area is fragile.

## Why it matters

Kilimanjaro's ice is a visible sign of climate change. The mountain's forests, which supply water to communities below, are even more important for the region.

## See it for yourself

Seeing the glaciers is, for many climbers, one of the most moving moments of the climb. [Plan your climb](/travel-proposal/).
